physicalContacts.scope: Passive native surface lattice: independently compressible box faces and translating curved surface cells backed by smaller hard cores. Springs and damping transfer collision reactions to free articulated bones; all cells retain actual position and velocity. This is a coarse engineering approximation, not volumetric anatomical skin, calibrated tissue or muscle simulation. Verified limb vertices use padded convex hulls with inward-offset hard cores. Feet divide the same outer convex volume into heel and medial/lateral forefoot cells for independent native load accommodation; the measured head and trunk use four disjoint anterior/posterior and left/right cells. Other measured segments use one three-axis passive shell. These compact cells can translate and shear but do not represent independent local compression on every opposing surface.

assessment.scope: Measured native floor loads and COM projection over actual loaded contacts. Expected support is task-specific; an allowed hand/knee contact is not automatically a loss of balance. Geometric margin is not a dynamic success certificate.

Springs and damping transfer collision reactions to free articulated bones; all cells retain actual position and velocity. This is a coarse engineering approximation, not volumetric anatomical skin, calibrated tissue or muscle simulation. Verified limb vertices use padded convex hulls with inward-offset hard cores. Feet divide the same outer convex volume into heel and medial/lateral forefoot cells for independent native load accommodation; the measured head and trunk use four disjoint anterior/posterior and left/right cells. Other measured segments use one three-axis passive shell. These compact cells can translate and shear but do not represent independent local compression on every opposing surface.

physicalContacts.scope: Passive native surface lattice: independently compressible box faces and translating curved surface cells backed by smaller hard cores. Springs and damping transfer collision reactions to free articulated bones; all cells retain actual position and velocity. This is a coarse engineering approximation, not volumetric anatomical skin, calibrated tissue or muscle simulation. Verified limb vertices use padded convex hulls with inward-offset hard cores. Feet divide the same outer convex volume into heel and medial/lateral forefoot cells for independent native load accommodation; the measured head and trunk use four disjoint anterior/posterior and left/right cells. Other measured segments use one three-axis passive shell. These compact cells can translate and shear but do not represent independent local compression on every opposing surface.

contactModel.assumptions: Layer thickness up to 8 mm (4 mm hands/feet), stiffness 50 kN/m per cell (120 kN/m feet), damping time 2 ms, 2% segment mass redistributed to cells, no numerical slide armature. Curved cells permit bounded shear/translation; box faces permit normal compression. Adjacent proxy overlap is deliberately not scored as self-collision. Consumers without verified measured source frames retain their declared primitive envelopes; those surfaces do not establish complete source-skin coverage. Measured convex profiles replace limb bounding primitives only for SHA-bound source fixtures. Every sampled majority-weight vertex is enclosed. Supporting planes retain 3 mm padding except the plantar plane, which trims only artificial padding below the observed lowest sole point (explicit zero sole padding). The hard core retains the same 4 mm inward plantar offset. Original segment inertia shapes and total mass are retained; convex collision surfaces do not silently refit mass or bone positions. Each plantar cell retains 120 kN/m stiffness and 4 mm travel, with tissue mass shared between the three cells. Shared internal partition faces are same-owner exclusions, not extra exterior volume.

upperContactCoverage.scope: Measured hands include all neutral finger-chain vertices as one envelope attached to the Hand body. Fingers have no independent native joints/contact; authored finger curls can leave this neutral envelope. Primitives without a verified neutral source binding do not establish complete hand/forearm skin coverage.

coreContactCoverage.scope: SHA-bound neutral head vertices and torso triangles replace bounding boxes with padded convex surfaces. Torso triangles are clipped at summed torso influence 0.5 and shared neutral joint heights, retaining mixed-weight waist skin and an independent lumbar surface. Padding, tissue stiffness/travel, total segment mass, collision exclusions and failure thresholds are unchanged. The neutral hull is partitioned into four independently translating anterior/posterior and left/right cells; it does not reproduce every skin deformation or anatomical concavity. Torso boundary cuts are enclosed by both neighbors in neutral. Posed seam continuity is not inferred. Neck surfaces remain declared primitives.

physicalContacts.scope: Passive native surface lattice: independently compressible box faces and translating curved surface cells backed by smaller hard cores. Springs and damping transfer collision reactions to free articulated bones; all cells retain actual position and velocity. This is a coarse engineering approximation, not volumetric anatomical skin, calibrated tissue or muscle simulation. Verified limb vertices use padded convex hulls with inward-offset hard cores. Feet divide the same outer convex volume into heel and medial/lateral forefoot cells for independent native load accommodation; the measured head and trunk use four disjoint anterior/posterior and left/right cells. Other measured segments use one three-axis passive shell. These compact cells can translate and shear but do not represent independent local compression on every opposing surface.

assessment.scope: Measured native floor loads and COM projection over actual loaded contacts. Expected support is task-specific; an allowed hand/knee contact is not automatically a loss of balance. Geometric margin is not a dynamic success certificate.

physicalContacts.scope: Passive native surface lattice: independently compressible box faces and translating curved surface cells backed by smaller hard cores. Springs and damping transfer collision reactions to free articulated bones; all cells retain actual position and velocity. This is a coarse engineering approximation, not volumetric anatomical skin, calibrated tissue or muscle simulation. Verified limb vertices use padded convex hulls with inward-offset hard cores. Feet divide the same outer convex volume into heel and medial/lateral forefoot cells for independent native load accommodation; the measured head and trunk use four disjoint anterior/posterior and left/right cells. Other measured segments use one three-axis passive shell. These compact cells can translate and shear but do not represent independent local compression on every opposing surface.

assessment.scope: Measured native floor loads and COM projection over actual loaded contacts. Expected support is task-specific; an allowed hand/knee contact is not automatically a loss of balance. Geometric margin is not a dynamic success certificate.

balanceControl.interpretation: COM feedback is an actuator request, not an external support force. Projection margin is geometric, not a dynamic stability guarantee.
balanceControl.scope: Approximate capture point from measured COM velocity and loaded floor contacts. Conflicting pose requests can yield with a measured support area; point/line support retains existing COM feedback without extra pose release. Gravity compensation and joint velocity tracking remain active. Authored timing is retained. No stepping or guaranteed recovery.
balanceControl.contributionScope: Incremental change in the final capped motor command from COM feedback and releasing opposing pose torque. This is not total motor torque or an externally applied body force.

stanceControl.interpretation: Local weighted sticking-contact approximation for actuator control; no solved-root correction or external support wrench.

supportEvents.sampling: Every native step; raw force and physical gates remain unchanged

physicalContacts.scope: Passive native surface lattice: independently compressible box faces and translating curved surface cells backed by smaller hard cores. Springs and damping transfer collision reactions to free articulated bones; all cells retain actual position and velocity. This is a coarse engineering approximation, not volumetric anatomical skin, calibrated tissue or muscle simulation. Verified limb vertices use padded convex hulls with inward-offset hard cores. Feet divide the same outer convex volume into heel and medial/lateral forefoot cells for independent native load accommodation; the measured head and trunk use four disjoint anterior/posterior and left/right cells. Other measured segments use one three-axis passive shell. These compact cells can translate and shear but do not represent independent local compression on every opposing surface.

assessment.scope: Measured native floor loads and COM projection over actual loaded contacts. Expected support is task-specific; an allowed hand/knee contact is not automatically a loss of balance. Geometric margin is not a dynamic success certificate.

balanceControl.interpretation: COM feedback is an actuator request, not an external support force. Projection margin is geometric, not a dynamic stability guarantee.
balanceControl.scope: Approximate capture point from measured COM velocity and loaded floor contacts. Conflicting pose requests can yield with a measured support area; point/line support retains existing COM feedback without extra pose release. Gravity compensation and joint velocity tracking remain active. Authored timing is retained. No stepping or guaranteed recovery.
balanceControl.contributionScope: Incremental change in the final capped motor command from COM feedback and releasing opposing pose torque. This is not total motor torque or an externally applied body force.

stanceControl.interpretation: Local weighted sticking-contact approximation for actuator control; no solved-root correction or external support wrench.

armFeasibility.scope: Experimental calibrated forearm axis and complete signed humeral rotation chart. Clinical thorax-frame bounds and the existing girdle-proxy budget are monitored on source, fitted intent and every achieved native step. An inadmissible state stops the trial; it is not projected away. This is monitored admissibility, not passive coupled anatomical stops. Other joint topology, mechanical ranges, force caps and tracking gates are unchanged.

initialization.scope: Retargeted source setup initializes native state once. A signed vertical rigid-envelope fit places the lowest native contact surface 1 mm above the floor; source world goals remain unchanged and their initial mismatch is measured. Gravity, native contact and bounded motor torques determine all later motion.

assessment.capacityAssumptions: Shared85 Nm hip-abduction reference for both body models, informed by measured62–65 Nm native static support demand. Other existing standing/neutral arm/trunk/toe caps retained. Control multiplies every native torque limit by0.55 at unchanged ranges and inertias.

capacityReference.calibration: Shared engineering reference for both visual body models, not a measured individual or sex-specific capability. A source-bound static single-leg target requires approximately 62–65 Nm at the supporting hip; the previous 35 Nm cap was below that task demand.
capacityReference.sourceScope: Small adult study reported female hip-abduction peak 86±21 Nm and male 140±44 Nm. These population measurements motivate a conservative shared 85 Nm reference; they do not validate this rig or movement.

assessment.controllerScope: Every native joint has bounded active posture and velocity tracking. restingPositionPolicy.scope: During a stationary captured Prone interval, reduced joint tone and damping allow gravity to load the floor. Anti-gravity bias and world-pose/COM task requests yield. contactModel.assumptions: Layer thickness up to 8 mm (4 mm hands/feet), stiffness 50 kN/m per cell (120 kN/m feet), damping time 2 ms, 2% segment mass redistributed to cells, no numerical slide armature. Curved cells permit bounded shear/translation; box faces permit normal compression. Adjacent proxy overlap is deliberately not scored as self-collision. Consumers without verified measured source frames retain their declared primitive envelopes; those surfaces do not establish complete source-skin coverage. Measured convex profiles replace limb bounding primitives only for SHA-bound source fixtures. Every sampled majority-weight vertex is enclosed. Supporting planes retain 3 mm padding except the plantar plane, which trims only artificial padding below the observed lowest sole point (explicit zero sole padding). The hard core retains the same 4 mm inward plantar offset. Original segment inertia shapes and total mass are retained; convex collision surfaces do not silently refit mass or bone positions. Each plantar cell retains 120 kN/m stiffness and 4 mm travel, with tissue mass shared between the three cells. Shared internal partition faces are same-owner exclusions, not extra exterior volume.

upperContactCoverage.scope: Measured hands include all neutral finger-chain vertices as one envelope attached to the Hand body. Fingers have no independent native joints/contact; authored finger curls can leave this neutral envelope. Primitives without a verified neutral source binding do not establish complete hand/forearm skin coverage.

coreContactCoverage.scope: SHA-bound neutral head vertices and torso triangles replace bounding boxes with padded convex surfaces. Torso triangles are clipped at summed torso influence 0.5 and shared neutral joint heights, retaining mixed-weight waist skin and an independent lumbar surface. Padding, tissue stiffness/travel, total segment mass, collision exclusions and failure thresholds are unchanged. The neutral hull is partitioned into four independently translating anterior/posterior and left/right cells; it does not reproduce every skin deformation or anatomical concavity. Torso boundary cuts are enclosed by both neighbors in neutral. Posed seam continuity is not inferred. Neck surfaces remain declared primitives.

centralSupport.scope: Exactly representable, in-range central source chain retained during floor-support limb fitting. Native dynamics remain free to depart from this intended pose.

physicalContacts.scope: Passive native surface lattice: independently compressible box faces and translating curved surface cells backed by smaller hard cores. Springs and damping transfer collision reactions to free articulated bones; all cells retain actual position and velocity. This is a coarse engineering approximation, not volumetric anatomical skin, calibrated tissue or muscle simulation. Verified limb vertices use padded convex hulls with inward-offset hard cores. Feet divide the same outer convex volume into heel and medial/lateral forefoot cells for independent native load accommodation; the measured head and trunk use four disjoint anterior/posterior and left/right cells. Other measured segments use one three-axis passive shell. These compact cells can translate and shear but do not represent independent local compression on every opposing surface.

assessment.scope: Measured native floor loads and COM projection over actual loaded contacts. Expected support is task-specific; an allowed hand/knee contact is not automatically a loss of balance. Geometric margin is not a dynamic success certificate.
